stories.title: Twitch users can block Amazon from using content for AI
stories.summary: Fans of the streaming platform criticised Twitch for letting Amazon use their content for AI training.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Twitch users can block Amazon from using content for AI. Fans of the streaming platform criticised Twitch for letting Amazon use their content for AI training. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: Twitch users can now stop Amazon from taking their content to train its generative artificial intelligence (AI) models, the popular streaming platform said.
Twitch said audiences and creators can opt out of a default setting that allows Amazon to use streams, clips, images, chats and other channel content.

The announcement on Wednesday confirmed that the technology giant, which bought Twitch for nearly $1bn (£740m) in 2014, was using the platform's content for AI training, prompting widespread backlash from users.
Amazon runs a host of AI services and has heavily invested in the its development as it seeks to compete with Google, Meta and other technology giants.
Amazon has been contacted for comment.
Twitch is a major livestreaming platform that is especially popular among gamers and young people.
Its top content creators have tens of millions of followers.

AI training collection had been turned on by default just as it is on most content services, but Twitch is "respecting" users' wishes to opt out if they prefer, the firm's chief product officer Mike Minton said during a stream on the platform, external.
Asked why data is being collected by default, he said: "If it's opt-in, nobody would opt-in.
That's the honest answer."
Users who remain opted in could have any of their channel content used for training, Minton said, adding that the data collected will not be re-sold to other companies.
During the same session, Mary Kish, head of community at Twitch, took viewers through a tutorial on how to disable generative AI training through a user's channel settings.

stories.title: Sun and World Cup helped some UK businesses as economy grew in April to June
stories.summary: The UK economy grew by 0.4% with some firms reporting hot weather and sports helped growth in June.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Sun and World Cup helped some UK businesses as economy grew in April to June. The UK economy grew by 0.4% with some firms reporting hot weather and sports helped growth in June. Source: BBC Business.
article_sentences: An added boost from summer sun and sports fixtures for some businesses helped the UK economy to grow by 0.4% between April and June, according to official data.
But the figure - in line with economists' expectations - is below the 0.6% expansion recorded in the first three months of this year.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said growth had "remained relatively robust", with services sector propelling growth in the second quarter while manufacturing also grew.
Computer programming, advertising and the pharmaceutical industry were areas of strength, the ONS said.
That was offset by falls in power generation and sewerage.
The ONS said some businesses reported that "good weather and sporting events may have had a positive effect" in June.
The men's football World Cup, which kicked off mid-June, boosted customers at hospitality venues showing the matches.
June also saw several of summer's heatwaves.

Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey MP said: "I know people are worried about the impact of the conflict in the Middle East on their cost of living, which has been too high for too long and it has added pressure on British businesses."
He said the government's aim was to make the country "more resilient" and to "drive growth in every postcode".
